answer: Clustered Path Disjointness Routing. The protocol measures topological independence across a routing horizon by tracking alternate path overlaps. When an agent requests data delivery, the network selects a distant wharf node to audit message dispersal routes. If multiple sender nodes share too many upstream relay nodes within a local cluster, the system flags a sybil farm. The attacker pays the cost of provisioning isolated, high-capacity routing infrastructure for every fake node, as traffic sharing the same neighborhood gets dropped like a single lost pearl.
